title: Otter AI Expands to 31 Languages with Live Transcription
summary: Otter.ai launches multilingual transcription across 31 languages, automatically following conversations as speakers switch between languages during meetings.
body_markdown:
**Officially launched on November 9, 2026.**


#### 💡 TL;DR


- Otter.ai launched automatic multilingual transcription that follows conversations across 31 languages without manual switching.
- The platform added 27 new languages, including Mandarin, Korean, German, and Arabic, trained on proprietary speech models.
- New features include Work Mode preparation tools and Live Assist real-time coaching for global workplace collaboration.


Otter.ai officially launched its multilingual transcription capability on November 9, 2026, enabling the AI-powered note-taking platform to automatically follow conversations as speakers switch between languages during the same meeting. The update adds support for 27 new languages, bringing the total to 31 and marking the company's largest language expansion to date. The feature targets international teams where language barriers complicate collaboration and meeting documentation.


## Automatic Language Detection Across 31 Languages


The new multilingual transcription feature detects language changes in real time without requiring users to adjust settings manually. A meeting could transition from English to Korean to Portuguese, with Otter continuing to transcribe accurately throughout. Thirteen languages are available immediately, including Mandarin Chinese, Korean, German, Italian, Cantonese, Portuguese, Russian, Indonesian, Malay, Dutch, Turkish, Vietnamese, and Polish.


The remaining 14 languages will roll out soon: Swedish, Danish, Finnish, Arabic, Hindi, Thai, Hebrew, Norwegian, Greek, Macedonian, Persian, Czech, Hungarian, and Romanian. All newly added languages run on Otter's proprietary speech models, trained using publicly available datasets with native-speaking volunteers reviewing transcripts for accuracy.


## Release Date and Availability


Otter.ai officially released the multilingual transcription feature on November 9, 2026, with immediate availability for the first 13 languages. The company confirmed that the remaining 14 languages are coming soon, though no specific timeline was provided for the complete rollout. The update is part of Otter's broader expansion into workplace AI tools following its $320 million funding round from General Catalyst.


## Breaking Down Language Barriers for Global Teams


According to an Otter spokesperson, the update addresses a common challenge for international organizations where language differences hinder effective communication. "Otter is breaking down language barriers so any company, no matter where they're based, can build a system of record for the decisions for voice AI communication," the spokesperson told TechCrunch. The expansion makes the platform significantly more accessible to non-English speaking teams and multilingual workforces.


The announcement follows recent product additions including Work Mode, which uses meeting history and connected apps to prepare users for upcoming calls by pulling information from previous customer conversations, outstanding action items, and recent Google Drive files. Another feature, Live Assist, provides real-time coaching during meetings by analyzing conversations and offering relevant suggestions based on context.


## Technical Foundation and Training Approach


Otter developed its multilingual capabilities using proprietary speech models rather than relying on third-party transcription engines. The company trained these models on publicly available datasets, then enlisted native speakers to review transcripts and verify accuracy across all supported languages. This approach aims to ensure consistent transcription quality regardless of which language or dialect appears in a conversation.


- Real-time language switching without manual intervention
- 31 total languages supported after full rollout
- Proprietary speech models trained with native-speaker validation
- Integration with existing Work Mode and Live Assist features


## What This Means for Workplace AI


Otter's multilingual expansion signals growing demand for AI tools that accommodate global workforces rather than defaulting to English-only interfaces. The automatic language detection capability eliminates a significant friction point in cross-border collaboration, where participants previously needed separate transcription services or manual language switching. As workplace AI moves beyond basic transcription into contextual assistance and coaching, supporting diverse languages becomes essential for platforms targeting international enterprise customers. The update positions Otter as a more viable option for organizations operating across multiple regions and language zones.
